messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Help with lavaan syntax: How can I prevent lavaan from automatically covariating all my variables?
parts: You seem to contradict yourself.  You either want a covariance to be fixed to zero (or some other value, like its observed sample statistic) or you want it to be freely estimated.  You seem to want both at the same time.
When I just enter the regressions line, lavaan automatically assumes a covariance between all my variables,
No, it just estimates them (if fixed.x = FALSE), in which case the estimate can be zero, or it fixes them to their observed sample statistics (if fixed.x = TRUE).
which is not theoretically correct for my model.
What does that mean?  Does your theory state they are exactly zero?
I prefer if lavaan would not do that and I specify the covariances manually.

Then use the lavaan() function instead of sem().  The latter turns on some "auto.*" arguments you can read about in the ?lavOptions help page.  But lavaan() will (by default) only estimate the parameters you tell it to.
I tried to set the covariation between variables of the three groups to zero, but the output does not look OK to me.
Can you be more specific? I imagine the model fits very poorly if the observed covariances are not the values (0) you fixed them to.
Basically, this way all covariances between all my variables are set to zero, which is not what I want.

Then I would just specify the model parameters you want to estimate, leave the rest fixed to zero (which is what "not specifying" them means), and use the lavaan() function.
